chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Ubeyda who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a mother of a child of his, and from her was a boy for him. So when death presented itself to him, he bequeathed to her two thousand Dirhams, or more. Is it for the inheritors that they enslave her? He (peace be upon him) said: No, but she would be emancipated from a third of the deceased (legacy), and she would be given whatever was bequeathed to her by it.
And in the Book of Al-Abbas, she would be emancipated from the share of her son, and she would be given from his third whatever he had bequeathed to her by it.

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (concubine who bears her master a child)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Umm al-Walad who is bequeathed money in a will?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific legal status of an 'Umm al-Walad' upon her master's death, ruling that she is emancipated directly from the one-third portion of the estate reserved for bequests rather than being absorbed into the general inheritance. The narration further specifies that her manumission is deducted from her son's share of the estate, highlighting the interplay between bequest laws and inheritance rights in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that a master's bequest for her freedom takes precedence, ensuring her transition from slavery to free status is funded by the estate's discretionary portion.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Abu Ubeyda who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had a mother of a child of his, and from her was a boy for him. So when the death presented itself to him, he bequeathed to her with two thousand Dirhams, or more. Is it for the inheritors that they enslave her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but she would be emancipated from a third of the deceased (legacy), and she would be given whatever was bequeathed to her by it’.
And in the Book of Al-Abbas, ‘She would be emancipated from the share of her son, and she would be given from his third whatever he had bequeathed to her by it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from abu ‘ Ubaydah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who had a mother of a child from whom he had a boy; and at the time of his death, willed for her two thousand or more; if the heirs can keep her as a slave-girl. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, they cannot keep her as a slave.
She becomes free in one-third of the legacy of the deceased and receives what is willed for her.’
“In the book of al- ‘Abbas it is said that she is freed from the share of her son and what is willed for her is given from the one-third of his legacy.”
